title: Blockchain Developer
description: Comprehensive curriculum covering cryptography, EVM architecture, Solidity, ERC standards, Foundry, Web3 frontends, smart contract security, DeFi protocols, L2 rollups, and zero-knowledge proofs.

phases.title: Cryptographic & EVM Foundations
phases.focus: Cryptography, Merkle Trees, Consensus (PoW/PoS), EVM Gas & State Mechanics

phases.title: Smart Contract Core & Tooling
phases.focus: Solidity, ERC Tokens, Foundry/Hardhat, Web3 Frontends & Reentrancy Security

phases.title: DeFi, Oracles & Scaling
phases.focus: AMMs, Chainlink Oracles, Layer 2 Rollups, ZKPs, Subgraphs & Smart Contract Auditing

phases.title: Governance, MEV & Protocol Capstone
phases.focus: DAOs, Multi-Sig Security, MEV Searchers, and Production DApp Launch

nodes.title: Cryptographic Foundations of Blockchains
nodes.subtitle: Cryptographic hashes (SHA-256, Keccak-256), public-key cryptography (secp256k1), digital signatures
learning_objectives: Explain how asymmetric key pairs (private/public key) enable trustless digital signatures
Analyze cryptographic collision resistance and one-way hash properties
feynman_prompts: Explain how digital signatures verify the sender without revealing the private key.
key_misconceptions: Assuming blockchain encryption hides transaction amounts by default (public blockchains are transparent)

nodes.title: Distributed Ledgers & Merkle Trees
nodes.subtitle: Blocks, headers, Merkle roots, SPV proofs, transaction immutability, peer-to-peer gossip
learning_objectives: Construct a Merkle tree and generate lightweight cryptographic proofs of inclusion
Explain how peer-to-peer gossip networks propagate transactions without a central coordinator
feynman_prompts: Why does tampering with a transaction in an early block invalidate all subsequent block hashes?
key_misconceptions: Believing a Merkle tree stores the entire database rather than cryptographic verification fingerprints

nodes.title: Consensus Mechanisms (PoW, PoS & BFT)
nodes.subtitle: Proof of Work (difficulty adjustment, 51% attack), Proof of Stake (slashing, validators, finality), BFT
learning_objectives: Contrast the resource incentives of Proof of Work with Proof of Stake slashing conditions
Explain Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) and the 2/3 validator consensus requirement
feynman_prompts: What prevents a rich validator from reversing transactions in Proof of Stake?
key_misconceptions: Assuming Proof of Stake has zero environmental or financial security cost

nodes.title: Ethereum & EVM Architecture
nodes.subtitle: EVM state machine, gas mechanics, opcodes, memory vs storage vs calldata, account model vs UTXO
learning_objectives: Model Ethereum state transitions, account nonce management, and gas calculation
Distinguish EVM memory (ephemeral) from storage (persistent, expensive) and calldata (read-only)
feynman_prompts: Why is writing to EVM storage significantly more expensive in gas than reading from memory?
key_misconceptions: Confusing Bitcoin's UTXO model with Ethereum's account-based state model

nodes.title: Solidity Smart Contract Fundamentals
nodes.subtitle: Data types, mappings, structs, modifiers, visibility (public, external, internal, private), constructors
learning_objectives: Write clean Solidity smart contracts with proper visibility modifiers and custom error types
Manage contract state variables and enforce access control with custom modifiers
feynman_prompts: Explain why custom errors (`error Unauthorized()`) save gas compared to `require(..., 'string')`.
key_misconceptions: Assuming `private` variables in Solidity cannot be read by anyone (all blockchain data is public)

nodes.title: ERC Token Standards (ERC-20, ERC-721, ERC-1155)
nodes.subtitle: ERC-20 fungible tokens, ERC-721 non-fungible tokens, ERC-1155 multi-tokens, safeTransferFrom, approvals
learning_objectives: Implement secure ERC-20 and ERC-721 tokens utilizing OpenZeppelin contracts
Safely handle token approval mechanics and prevent allowance race conditions
feynman_prompts: Why is the standard `approve` and `transferFrom` two-step pattern required for smart contract interaction?
key_misconceptions: Assuming transferring NFTs is fundamentally different from updating a mapping index

nodes.title: Development Toolchains: Foundry & Hardhat
nodes.subtitle: Forge, Anvil, Cast, Solidity-based testing, fuzz testing, deployment scripts, gas profiling
learning_objectives: Write fast unit and fuzz tests in Foundry using native Solidity
Profile contract gas consumption and simulate deployments against local Anvil forks
feynman_prompts: Why is fuzz testing in Foundry superior to hardcoded unit test assertions for math edge cases?
key_misconceptions: Deploying smart contracts to mainnet without extensive local test suite simulation

nodes.title: Web3 Frontend Integration (viem, wagmi, ethers)
nodes.subtitle: Wallet connection (MetaMask, WalletConnect), provider vs signer, ABI encoding, transaction receipts
learning_objectives: Connect modern frontend apps to Ethereum nodes using viem and wagmi React hooks
Handle pending transaction states, gas estimations, and user signature rejections gracefully
feynman_prompts: Explain the difference between a read-only node call (`eth_call`) and a state-modifying transaction (`eth_sendRawTransaction`).
key_misconceptions: Assuming transaction submission guarantees immediate state confirmation without waiting for block receipts

nodes.title: Smart Contract Security & Attack Vectors
nodes.subtitle: Reentrancy attacks, integer overflow, flash loan exploits, frontrunning/MEV, access control flaws
learning_objectives: Identify and remediate reentrancy vulnerabilities using Checks-Effects-Interactions and ReentrancyGuard
Protect contracts against sandwich attacks and frontrunning price manipulations
feynman_prompts: Walk through how the classic DAO reentrancy exploit worked line by line.
key_misconceptions: Believing that using modern Solidity >=0.8 automatic overflow checks solves all security vulnerabilities

nodes.title: DeFi Primitives: AMMs & Lending Protocols
nodes.subtitle: Automated Market Makers (x*y=k), liquidity pools, impermanent loss, collateralized lending, liquidations
learning_objectives: Deconstruct the constant product formula (x * y = k) used by Uniswap v2
Calculate impermanent loss and model collateralization ratios for decentralized lending
feynman_prompts: Explain why impermanent loss occurs for liquidity providers when prices diverge.
key_misconceptions: Assuming automated market makers have zero slippage for large orders

nodes.title: Decentralized Oracles & Chainlink
nodes.subtitle: The Oracle problem, Chainlink price feeds, VRF (verifiable random function), CCIP, staleness checks
learning_objectives: Integrate Chainlink price feeds with heartbeat and round staleness validation checks
Generate provably fair random numbers in smart contracts using Chainlink VRF v2
feynman_prompts: Why cannot a smart contract make a direct HTTP request to fetch an off-chain stock price?
key_misconceptions: Failing to validate price feed round timestamp, leading to stale pricing exploits

nodes.title: Layer 2 Scaling: Optimistic & ZK Rollups
nodes.subtitle: State bloat, Optimistic Rollups (Arbitrum, Optimism, fraud proofs), ZK-Rollups (Starknet, zkSync, validity proofs)
learning_objectives: Explain the architectural difference between fraud proofs (optimistic) and validity proofs (zero-knowledge)
Bridge assets and interact with smart contracts on Layer 2 networks
feynman_prompts: Why do Optimistic Rollups have a 7-day challenge window for mainnet withdrawals while ZK-Rollups do not?
key_misconceptions: Assuming Layer 2 networks operate as completely separate independent blockchains without L1 security

nodes.title: Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKP) Fundamentals
nodes.subtitle: zk-SNARKs, zk-STARKs, arithmetic circuits, Circom, non-interactive proofs, privacy & verification
learning_objectives: Author basic arithmetic circuits in Circom to generate verifiable proofs of knowledge
Verify zero-knowledge proofs on-chain inside a Solidity smart contract
feynman_prompts: Explain how a zero-knowledge proof proves knowledge of a secret without revealing the secret.
key_misconceptions: Confusing zero-knowledge data privacy with data encryption

nodes.title: Decentralized Storage & Indexing (IPFS, The Graph)
nodes.subtitle: IPFS content addressing (CIDs), Pinata/Filecoin, GraphQL subgraphs, indexing event logs
learning_objectives: Deploy Subgraphs on The Graph protocol to index and query contract event logs via GraphQL
Host metadata and immutable assets on IPFS using content identifiers (CIDs)
feynman_prompts: Why is querying contract state via a Graph indexer thousands of times faster than direct RPC node calls?
key_misconceptions: Storing large files or images directly on-chain inside EVM smart contract storage

nodes.title: Smart Contract Auditing & Static Analysis
nodes.subtitle: Slither, Mythril, Certora formal verification, manual audit methodology, creating audit reports
learning_objectives: Run static analysis tools (Slither, Mythril) in CI to detect vulnerabilities pre-deployment
Perform rigorous manual security code audits documenting vulnerability severity and remediation
feynman_prompts: What types of logical flaws can human manual auditing catch that automated scanners miss?
key_misconceptions: Assuming a 100% clean Slither static analysis run guarantees a contract is hack-proof

nodes.title: DAOs, Governance & Multi-Sig Infrastructure
nodes.subtitle: Safe (Gnosis Safe), timelocks, Governor contracts, quorum, voting weight, proposal lifecycles
learning_objectives: Deploy multi-signature treasury vaults using Safe and establish secure sign-off thresholds
Implement on-chain governance workflows with timelock delays to prevent flash loan hijacking
feynman_prompts: Why must on-chain governance proposals enforce an immutable timelock delay before execution?
key_misconceptions: Allowing immediate execution of governance proposals without timelock protection

nodes.title: MEV (Maximal Extractable Value) & Flashbots
nodes.subtitle: Searchers, builders, proposers, sandwich attacks, private mempools, Flashbots Protect, MEV-Boost
learning_objectives: Explain the MEV supply chain from searchers identifying arbitrage to block builders and validators
Protect user transactions from predatory frontrunning using private RPC endpoints and MEV-Boost
feynman_prompts: How do searchers use private mempools to execute atomic risk-free DEX arbitrage?
key_misconceptions: Assuming miners/validators only order transactions purely by gas fee timestamp

nodes.title: Full-Stack Web3 DApp Production Capstone
nodes.subtitle: End-to-end dApp: audited smart contracts, L2 deployment, subgraph indexing, wagmi UI, Safe treasury
learning_objectives: Architect and deploy an enterprise-grade decentralized protocol with multi-sig administration
Integrate automated CI testing, gas profiling, subgraph indexing, and production Web3 UI
feynman_prompts: What are the critical deployment checklist steps required before releasing contracts to Ethereum mainnet?
key_misconceptions: Failing to renounce ownership or transfer admin keys to a multi-sig vault post-deployment
